BiblicalUsage: Ramath-Lechi is a place in Palestine — the hill of the jawbone, where Samson threw down the jawbone of the ass with which he slew a thousand men. 'And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking, that he cast away the jawbone out of his hand, and called that place Ramath-lehi.'
TheologicalSignificance: The point for me is that the name is a trophy: Samson threw the weapon away and named the place for it, so that Israel would remember what God did with a jawbone.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
